steps.title: What Are Streams?
steps.text: Surgewave Streams is a stream processing library that lets you transform, aggregate, and join data in real time. It runs inside your .NET application with no external processing cluster required.

steps.title: Topology: Your Processing Graph
steps.text: A topology is a directed graph of processing nodes built with StreamsBuilder. Data flows from source topics through transformations (map, filter, groupBy) and into output topics or state stores.

steps.title: Stream vs Table
steps.text: A Stream represents an unbounded sequence of records (inserts). A Table represents the latest value per key (upserts). Streams are for events; Tables are for current state like inventory or user profiles.

steps.title: Windowing for Time-Based Aggregations
steps.text: Windows group records by time intervals. Tumbling windows are fixed and non-overlapping (hourly reports). Hopping windows overlap (moving averages). Session windows are gap-based (user sessions).

steps.title: State Stores
steps.text: State stores persist aggregation results locally. You can query them interactively for real-time lookups. Lesson 7.5 covers KeyValueStore, WindowStore, and interactive queries.
